That is a change to what the indicator MEANS, not to how it is measured, and belongs to the operator.", "decided_by": "RULE-A5-v1", "decision": "A covering sitemap is the SOLE pass path. A served llms.txt is recorded as evidence and cannot satisfy the leg on its own. Rationale: the sitemap is the only one of the three with a standardised way to assert that a specific URL is covered; llms.txt has no such semantics, and accepting its mere presence would score having the file rather than being discoverable. | rf_ask_plain | The site's sitemap files, the list of pages search engines routinely ask every site for. |
| rf_fail | For every data page looked at, the sitemaps served on the agency's own site were read and none lists the page's address in exactly the recorded form (a trailing slash, redirect target or query-string variant does not match), or the only discovery file served is an llms.txt (which by its proposal summarises a site rather than listing every page), or no sitemap is served at the standard locations; the reason names which. It is not a claim that the page is absent from the sitemap in every form, nor that search engines cannot find the page, because well-linked pages are found without a sitemap. |
| rf_fix_line | List the product address in the discovery file that is already served. |
| rf_hypothesis | Is the data page listed in the host's sitemap? Search engines and answer engines discover pages by following links and reading sitemaps; on a large site, a page a sitemap omits can go undiscovered, and an SI client cannot cite a page its retrieval layer never found. |
| rf_name_brief | The data page is in the site's sitemap |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not read one or more of the discovery files, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client, the client's own robots.txt compliance kept it from reading the file, or it could not confirm an absence or hit a server or network error. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages are listed in a served sitemap and some are not. |
| rf_pass | Every data page looked at was found listed: a sitemap served on the agency's own site carries the page's address exactly as the diagnostic records it. |
| rf_plain_name | The site's sitemap lists the data page |
| rf_question | Is the agency's data page listed in a sitemap served on the agency's own website? |
